out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: Time as a Public Health Control, Written Procedures
violations.observation: The person in charge is not able to provide written procedures for the use of time as a public health control with the following time/temperature control for safety food item(s): Sushi rice (acidified).
violations.corrective_action: If time only is used as a public health control for a working supply of time/temperature control for safety food before cooking or for ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that is displayed or held for service for immediate consumption, written procedures shall be prepared in advance and maintained in the food establishment and made available to the regulatory authority upon request. PIC agreed to use TPHC for the sushi rice and to maintain documentation for the initial temperature and the time the rice is discarded. EHS provided a copy of TPHC agreement to PIC.

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: Observed raw scallops thawing at room temperature in a container on the kitchen prep table.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. PIC understands thawing food should be cooked from frozen, thaw under continuous running water, or put in a refrigerator to thaw. PIC completely submerged raw scallops under running water.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Observed cups without handle using as a dispensing utensils inside all rice warmers.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. PIC removed the cups from rice warmers and understands dispensing utensils should have a handle if stored inside food items. CHOPSTICKS (Inspection Date: 07/23/2026) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Manufacturer containers of Granulated Chicken Flavor Soup Base Mix were observed reused for the storage of MSG (monosodium glutamate) and fresh belt pepper.
violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers may not be reused for secondary storage of other foods because the containers are not durable enough for multiple reuse and become uncleanable. EHS instructed the manager that these types of containers are not designed for the continuous ware washing process. They can be used for sanitizer buckets for towels. PIC corrected the violation by transferring the MSG and fresh green pepper into approved, reusable food-grade containers.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Durable/Smooth Materials
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surface of the following equipment is not corrosion resistant, nonabsorbent, and/or smooth: Observed cardboard on the kitchen’s shelves.
violations.corrective_action: Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other foods that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a corrosion- resistant, nonabsorbent, and smooth material. PIC discarded cardboard and thoroughly cleaned the kitchen shelves.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: Observed raw beef stored above cooked noodles in WIC.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. PIC rearranged food items: PIC placed raw beef below cooked noodles.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Storage of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed that poisonous and toxic materials are not properly stored to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens or single service items. Observed WD-40 stored among food items on the prep table in the back kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored below food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items to prevent contamination. EHS discussed proper storage of chemicals, sanitizers, table cleaners, etc. They shall be stored away from or separated from any clean equipment, clean utensils, and dry foods. PIC relocated WD-40 to the designated chemical storage area.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: working containers of various spices at cook line.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EHS discussed proper labeling of working containers, bottles, etc. PIC labeled all working containers during inspection.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food items were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: OBSERVED BEAN SPROUTS AT 69F, THAI RED CURRY SAUCE AT 73F, SHREDDED CABBAGE AT 72F, AND SHREDDED CABBAGE #2 AT 74F IN 3-DOOR PREP TOP.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. A TECHNICIAN HAD BEEN CALLED TO REPAIR COLD HOLDING BEFORE INSPECTION. PLEASE EMAIL EHS WHEN UNIT HAS BEEN REPAIRED.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: OBSERVED BATCHES OF FRIED CHICKEN IN 1-DOOR UPR COOLER AND WALK-IN COOLER MADE THE DAY PRIOR TO INSPECTION WITHOUT A DATE MARKING.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. PIC ADDED DATE MARKING DURING INSPECTION. PIC UNDERSTANDS ALL PREPARED/COOKED TCS FOODS MUST BE LABELED IF THE FACILITY IS KEEPING THEM FOR MORE THAN 24 HOURS. PIC INFORMED EHS MOST PREPARED FOODS IN ESTABLISHMENT ARE NOT KEPT FOR MORE THAN 24 HOURS.
